svg.title: What JCI adds: resolving an internal causal endpoint
svg.desc: Synthetic soft_direct evidence. The true mechanism C to X to Y and Z to Y generates 1000 independent rows per repetition. Without JCI assumptions, FCI returns X circle-arrow Y in 20 of 20 repetitions. JCI1 and JCI12 each return X arrow Y in 20 of 20 repetitions. At 200 rows each JCI setting recovers both endpoints in 16 of 20 repetitions.
svg.text: What JCI adds: resolving an internal causal endpoint
Synthetic soft_direct | C: randomized context; X, Z, Y: system variables | n = 1,000 per repetition

svg.text: 20 / 20 repetitions
20 / 20 repetitions
C changes the probability of X:
The endpoint at X is unresolved.
An open circle records uncertainty.
Both methods use C, X, Z and Y.
The tail at X is resolved.
X is an ancestor of Y in the PAG.
JCI1 and JCI12 each give this result.
Ground truth used for validation only.
Only the queried X–Y edge is shown.
Blue marks the additional orientation.
Information supplied by the design
JCI1: system variables do not cause C. JCI2: C has no latent common cause with the system.
Mechanism: C and Y are dependent; C and Y are independent given X.
Observed increment: X-side endpoint resolution at n = 1,000; JCI1 already supplies the gain here.
At n = 200: 16/20 correct X–Y endpoint pairs for each JCI setting. Sample requirements are mechanism-specific.
Evidence: 20 independent synthetic datasets per sample size. The reported increment concerns structural identification in this mechanism.
Graphical style informed by Mooij, Magliacane & Claassen (JMLR, 2020). Experiment: structural-query-evidence, 2026-09-29.
